headline: UK firm ORCA Computing has launched its PT-3 light-based quantum computer in a London data centre, running alongside NVIDIA chips for science and optimisation work.
score_reason: Company launch with company-reported results; quantum advantage is a claim not independently shown.
importance_line: It offers businesses a quantum system next to ordinary AI hardware in a commercial data centre, which matters to drug and materials researchers, but the advantage claims are ORCA's own and have not been independently confirmed.
summary: The Quantum Insider reports, from an ORCA press release, that the PT-3 photonic quantum computer is live at Digital Realty's innovation lab in London, where ORCA says a hybrid version of NVIDIA's Proteina protein-design model raised the share of useful designs by 20% and an energy-scheduling task ran over 12 times faster than on its predecessor. ORCA calls it the first machine built for commercial quantum advantage, a claim that rests on the company's own tests.
notes: Computer Weekly blocked (403, Cloudflare); HPWire also blocked; read The Quantum Insider, which carries the ORCA press release. All figures are company claims.
